title: Netting Deductions and Corrections Into Qualifying Monthly Earnings
content:
The deductions and corrections booked to a Keyturn Host Payout Account in the twelve months up to that day are netted, and that net, taken at the offset share and spread evenly over twelve months, is added to the qualifying monthly earnings. Because deductions are booked as negative entries and corrections as positive ones, that net lowers the qualifying monthly earnings whenever deductions outweigh corrections and lifts them whenever corrections outweigh deductions. The sum added is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

The offset share turns on how the account settles and on whether its transfers have been coming back.

| How the account settles | Transfers come back unpaid in the twelve months up to that day | Offset share |
|---|---|---|
| Swept as each trip completes | None | 10 percent |
| Swept as each trip completes | One or more | 5 percent |
| Any other rhythm | Any | 0 percent |

## Points of judgement

**An account swept as each trip completes with a clean return record over that period.** The first row governs at 10 percent.

**The same account once a transfer has come back unpaid in that period.** The second row governs at 5 percent, and the number of returns beyond the first does not change it.

**An account settling on any other rhythm.** The third row governs whatever its return record, so nothing is netted into the qualifying monthly earnings.

## On hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical account whose deductions and corrections over the twelve months up to that day net to 12000.00 USD below nothing. The figure added to the qualifying monthly earnings is 100.00 USD below nothing in the first row, 50.00 USD below nothing in the second, and nothing at all in the third. Where instead those entries net to 2400.00 USD above nothing, the figure added is 20.00 USD in the first row, 10.00 USD in the second and nothing in the third.
